Rules.Name: Graphics/Compute Idle [%]
Explanation_Accumulated:
The gr__idle_cycles_pct metric measures the % of the elapsed cycles where the Compute/Graphics Engine is fully idle, with its pipeline fully empty.
If the GR Idle% is not close to 0%, the workload is likely starved by the CPU, or limited by DX12 Fence Wait calls, or by Copy Engine activity.  
If pcie__rx_requests_aperture_bar1_op_read.sum > 500, then CPU readbacks from CPU-Visible VRAM may be a problem.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
To investigate possible CPU side issues, we recommend using Nsight Systems:  
https://developer.nvidia.com/nsight-systems

Rules.Name: L1TEX L2 Hit Rates
Explanation_Accumulated:
If the L1TEX hit rate is poor, it causes more requests to go to the L2 cache.  
If the L2 hit rate is poor, it causes more requests to go to VRAM.  
A poor L2 hit rate is typically caused by the working set size of the GPU workload exceeding the L2 cache capacity.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
If the L1TEX hit rate is poor, the following changes may help:
- Enabling mipmapping and/or fetching coarser mip levels
- Using a smaller texture format (e.g. FP16 depths instead of FP32)
- Making adjacent pixels fetch closer texels in memory
- For PSs, increasing the triangle size if some triangles are sub-pixel
- For PSs, converting the PS to a CS and tweaking the thread group size
- For CSs, increasing the thread group size (see SIGGRAPH 2020 talk: https://developer.nvidia.com/siggraph/2020/video/sigg01)
- For CSs, if no async-compute queue is used, reducing the amount of allocated shared memory
If the L2 hit rate is poor:
  
  - For CSs with 2D thread groups, thread group ID swizzling may help (see https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/optimizing-compute-shaders-for-l2-locality-using-thread-group-id-swizzling/).
  - In all cases, fetching 2D textures using a larger LOD bias (to fetch coarser mip levels) may help.

Rules.Name: L1TEX Local Stores

Metrics.Name: L1TEX Tag-Stage Miss Sectors Local Store [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:
Local Memory stores may be caused by:
- Live-state spilling in DXR/VKR DispatchRays/TraceRays workloads
- Dynamically-indexed temp arrays
- Register spilling in graphics shaders
Suggestion_Accumulated:
If this is a DispatchRays workload, minimize live-state spilled bytes across TraceRay calls in the HLSL/GLSL by using the Nsight Graphics Shader Profiler. Variables initialized before a TraceRay or traceNV call and used after it are live state that needs to be maintained across the call while invoking hit and miss shaders.  
If you have dynamically indexed temp arrays (e.g. 'int array[64];'), you may want to try reducing its size and replacing the array accesses with immediate constants.

Explanation_Accumulated:
The percentages of maximum throughput per GPU sub-unit, sorted in decreasing order.  
If the top-SOL unit has a SOL% < 60%, the performance of this workload is latency-limited by that GPU unit.  
If the top-SOL unit has a SOL% > 80%, the performance of this workload is throughput-limited by that GPU unit.

Rules.Name: SM Warp Occupancy [Warps Per Cycle]
Explanation_Accumulated:
NVIDIA Ampere RTX GPUs have up to 48 warp slots per SM.  
NVIDIA Turing RTX GPUS have up to 32 warp slots per SM.  
Note: Increasing SM warp occupancy may not necessarily result in a performance gain.  
See https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/optimizing-vk-vkr-and-dx12-dxr-applications-using-nsight-graphics-gpu-trace-advanced-mode-metrics/ and https://www.gdcvault.com/browse/gdc-19/play/1026202.  
Less than 4 active warps per SM is a starving condition.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
The following strategies may be used to increase the SM warp occupancy:
- Reducing the SM warp launch stall reasons (see the SM Warp Occupancy section), typically register pressure
- Overlapping this workload with an indepedendent SM workload by using an Asynchronous Compute queue (for DX12 or VK)
- Reducing the number of DX12 ResouceBarriers or VK vkCmdPipelineBarrier commands

Rules.Name: Active Threads Per Warp

Metrics.Name: Thread Inst Executed Pred On per Inst Executed [%]
SM Thread Inst Executed Pred On

Explanation_Accumulated:
Low active threads per warp can be caused by:
- Divergent branches, where an if-statement's condition resolves to a mixture of true and false across threads in the warp.
- Divergent control flow within warps (such as dynamic loops with different loop counts per thread).
- Dispatch commands launching less than 32 threads per thread group.
- In DispatchRays/vkCmdTraceRays, different rays executing different hit shaders within the same warp.  
Thread execution divergence due to dynamic control flow increases warp latencies, since all partially-taken branches must be executed with masked-out threads.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
In general, try to make all threads of the same warp take the same control-flow decision (dynamic branches or loops).  
In RayGen shaders, using the Shader Execution Reordering (SER) NvAPI. See https://developer.nvidia.com/sites/default/files/akamai/gameworks/ser-whitepaper.pdf

Rules.Name: Warp Stalled by L1TEX Long Scoreboard

Metrics.Name: Warps Issue Stalled Long Scoreboard L1 [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:
Percentage of cumulative warp cycles for warps waiting on a dependency on a memory read from:
- textures or buffers (SRVs)
- surfaces (UAVs or ROVs)
- local or global memory
Suggestion_Accumulated:
Run the Shader Profiler and locate which HLSL/GLSL instructions are causing most long_scoreboard stalls on their dependent instructions.  
* Try better hiding the latency of the L1TEX instructions:  
  - With other math instructions: try hoisting L1TEX instructions (i.e.: prefetch: move the texture fetches so they happen earlier in the program)  
  - With other L1TEX instructions: try batching likely hits (e.g. by grouping independent texture fetches in batches of 2 to 4 back-to-back instructions at the HLSL level)  
  - Removing unnecessary control flow that prevents L1TEX instructions from being batched
* Try reducing the latencies of the L1TEX instructions:  
  - Consider using more compact texture formats and/or reducing texture sizes  
  - Consider using Buffer SRV Loads instead of Buffer UAV Loads  
  - Consider increasing the L1TEX and L2 hit rates (see the L1TEX L2 section)

Rules.Name: Warp Stalled by No Instruction
Explanation_Accumulated: Percentage of cumulative warp cycles for warps waiting to be selected for instruction fetch, or waiting on an instruction cache miss.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
Reducing the number of SASS instructions per shader may help (for instance, by not unrolling certain loops).  
Reducing the number of active shaders may help (for instance, by doing lighting in a raygen shader instead of in hit shaders).  
Reducing ray-latency divergence may help, for instance by shortening rays and falling back to IBL (see SIGGRAPH 2020 talk: https://developer.nvidia.com/siggraph/2020/video/sigg01).  
Note: As long as the instructions that are never hit are in large chunks, they should not take up space in the SM instruction cache.

Rules.Name: Warp Stalled by Immediate Cache Miss
Explanation_Accumulated: IMC-cache misses can originate from immediate-indexed constant-buffer loads or from bindless-header loads or texture-header loads.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
Run the Shader Profiler and locate which HLSL instructions have most imc_miss stalls.  
Avoiding frequent constant-buffer updates between draw/dispatch calls may help.

Rules.Name: SM Fully Idle

Metrics.Name: Unused Warp Slots in Idle SMs [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:
Percentage of the cycles where an SM has all of its warp slots empty (SM is fully idle).  
This may be due to the "Tail Effect", that is the warp occupancy going down at the end of a SM workload before a Wait For Idle.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
* Look at the SM Warp Occupancy metric graph in GPU Trace. If a significant tail is there, then:
  - See if a DX12 ResourceBarrier command can be removed at the end of the current workload, to let it execute concurrently with the next one, assuming that the current and next workloads are in the same subchannel (Graphics or Compute).
* If high, and resource dependencies permit, then:
  - If this workload is a Compute Shader, then it may be a good candidate for being moved to an async-compute queue.
  - If this workload is Graphics, then it may be a good candidate to be overlapped with async-compute work.

Rules.Name: SM Throughputs
Explanation_Accumulated:
SM pipes on GA10X and AD10X:  
- adu: Computed branches and indexed constants
- alu: INT32 except multiply; FP32 comparison
- cbu: Divergent branches and control flow
- fma: FP32 mul/add, FP16 mul/add
- fmaheavy: FP32 mul/add and INT32 multiply
- fp64: FP64 mul/add
- ipa: Pixel shader attribute interpolation
- lsu: Global, local, shared memory, and misc
- tensor: Tensor matrix multiply (FP16, INT8/4/1)
- tex: Texture and surface memory
- uniform: Warp-level scalar operations
- xu: Transcendentals and float/int conversion
Suggestion_Accumulated: Look at the top SM throughput metric and remove work from its associated pipe to get a speedup.

Rules.Name: Culling Rates
Explanation_Accumulated:
VPC (ViewPort Culling) happens right before Coarse Raster.  
ZCULL happens between Coarse Raster and Fine Raster.  
EarlyZ happens between FineRaster and the Pixel Shader execution.

Rules.Name: L2 Misses in System Memory
Explanation_Accumulated:
% of the L2 cycles with a pending miss in System Memory.  
L2 misses to System Memory (aka CPU memory) have a much higher latency than misses to VRAM.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
On DX11: Changing DYNAMIC (system memory) resources to DEFAULT (VRAM) resources may help.  
On DX12: Changing UPLOAD heaps (or POOL_L0 heaps) to CPU-Visible VRAM (via NVAPI) may help. See https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/optimizing-dx12-resource-uploads-to-the-gpu-using-cpu-visible-vram/.

- Enabling mipmapping and/or fetching coarser mip levels
- Using a smaller texture format (e.g. FP16 depths instead of FP32)
- Making adjacent pixels fetch closer texels in memory
- For PSs, increasing the triangle size if some triangles are sub-pixel

Rules.Name: L1TEX L2 Hit Rates
Explanation_Accumulated:
If the L1TEX hit rate is poor, it causes more requests to go to the L2 cache.  
If the L2 hit rate is poor, it causes more requests to go to VRAM.  
A poor L2 hit rate is typically caused by the working set size of the GPU workload exceeding the L2 cache capacity.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
If the L1TEX hit rate is poor, the following changes may help:
- Enabling mipmapping and/or fetching coarser mip levels
- Using a smaller texture format (e.g. FP16 depths instead of FP32)
- Making adjacent pixels fetch closer texels in memory
- For PSs, increasing the triangle size if some triangles are sub-pixel
- For PSs, converting the PS to a CS and tweaking the thread group size
- For CSs, increasing the thread group size (see SIGGRAPH 2020 talk: https://developer.nvidia.com/siggraph/2020/video/sigg01)
- For CSs, if no async-compute queue is used, reducing the amount of allocated shared memory
If the L2 hit rate is poor:
  
  - For CSs with 2D thread groups, thread group ID swizzling may help (see https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/optimizing-compute-shaders-for-l2-locality-using-thread-group-id-swizzling/).
  - In all cases, fetching 2D textures using a larger LOD bias (to fetch coarser mip levels) may help.

SM pipes on GA10X and AD10X:  
- adu: Computed branches and indexed constants
- alu: INT32 except multiply; FP32 comparison
- cbu: Divergent branches and control flow
- fma: FP32 mul/add, FP16 mul/add
- fmaheavy: FP32 mul/add and INT32 multiply
- fp64: FP64 mul/add
- ipa: Pixel shader attribute interpolation
- lsu: Global, local, shared memory, and misc
- tensor: Tensor matrix multiply (FP16, INT8/4/1)
- tex: Texture and surface memory
- uniform: Warp-level scalar operations
- xu: Transcendentals and float/int conversion
Suggestion_Accumulated: Look at the top SM throughput metric and remove work from its associated pipe to get a speedup.

Rules.Name: Graphics/Compute Idle [%]
Explanation_Accumulated:
The gr__idle_cycles_pct metric measures the % of the elapsed cycles where the Compute/Graphics Engine is fully idle, with its pipeline fully empty.
If the GR Idle% is not close to 0%, the workload is likely starved by the CPU, or limited by DX12 Fence Wait calls, or by Copy Engine activity.  
If pcie__rx_requests_aperture_bar1_op_read.sum > 500, then CPU readbacks from CPU-Visible VRAM may be a problem.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
To investigate possible CPU side issues, we recommend using Nsight Systems:  
https://developer.nvidia.com/nsight-systems

Rules.Name: L1TEX L2 Hit Rates
Explanation_Accumulated:
If the L1TEX hit rate is poor, it causes more requests to go to the L2 cache.  
If the L2 hit rate is poor, it causes more requests to go to VRAM.  
A poor L2 hit rate is typically caused by the working set size of the GPU workload exceeding the L2 cache capacity.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
If the L1TEX hit rate is poor, the following changes may help:
- Enabling mipmapping and/or fetching coarser mip levels
- Using a smaller texture format (e.g. FP16 depths instead of FP32)
- Making adjacent pixels fetch closer texels in memory
- For PSs, increasing the triangle size if some triangles are sub-pixel
- For PSs, converting the PS to a CS and tweaking the thread group size
- For CSs, increasing the thread group size (see SIGGRAPH 2020 talk: https://developer.nvidia.com/siggraph/2020/video/sigg01)
- For CSs, if no async-compute queue is used, reducing the amount of allocated shared memory
If the L2 hit rate is poor:
  
  - For CSs with 2D thread groups, thread group ID swizzling may help (see https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/optimizing-compute-shaders-for-l2-locality-using-thread-group-id-swizzling/).
  - In all cases, fetching 2D textures using a larger LOD bias (to fetch coarser mip levels) may help.

Rules.Name: L1TEX Local Stores

Metrics.Name: L1TEX Tag-Stage Miss Sectors Local Store [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:
Local Memory stores may be caused by:
- Live-state spilling in DXR/VKR DispatchRays/TraceRays workloads
- Dynamically-indexed temp arrays
- Register spilling in graphics shaders
Suggestion_Accumulated:
If this is a DispatchRays workload, minimize live-state spilled bytes across TraceRay calls in the HLSL/GLSL by using the Nsight Graphics Shader Profiler. Variables initialized before a TraceRay or traceNV call and used after it are live state that needs to be maintained across the call while invoking hit and miss shaders.  
If you have dynamically indexed temp arrays (e.g. 'int array[64];'), you may want to try reducing its size and replacing the array accesses with immediate constants.

Rules.Name: Active Threads Per Warp

Metrics.Name: Thread Inst Executed Pred On per Inst Executed [%]
SM Thread Inst Executed Pred On

Explanation_Accumulated:
Low active threads per warp can be caused by:
- Divergent branches, where an if-statement's condition resolves to a mixture of true and false across threads in the warp.
- Divergent control flow within warps (such as dynamic loops with different loop counts per thread).
- Dispatch commands launching less than 32 threads per thread group.
- In DispatchRays/vkCmdTraceRays, different rays executing different hit shaders within the same warp.  
Thread execution divergence due to dynamic control flow increases warp latencies, since all partially-taken branches must be executed with masked-out threads.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
In general, try to make all threads of the same warp take the same control-flow decision (dynamic branches or loops).  
In RayGen shaders, using the Shader Execution Reordering (SER) NvAPI. See https://developer.nvidia.com/sites/default/files/akamai/gameworks/ser-whitepaper.pdf

Rules.Name: SM Fully Idle

Metrics.Name: Unused Warp Slots in Idle SMs [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:
Percentage of the cycles where an SM has all of its warp slots empty (SM is fully idle).  
This may be due to the "Tail Effect", that is the warp occupancy going down at the end of a SM workload before a Wait For Idle.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
* Look at the SM Warp Occupancy metric graph in GPU Trace. If a significant tail is there, then:
  - See if a DX12 ResourceBarrier command can be removed at the end of the current workload, to let it execute concurrently with the next one, assuming that the current and next workloads are in the same subchannel (Graphics or Compute).
* If high, and resource dependencies permit, then:
  - If this workload is a Compute Shader, then it may be a good candidate for being moved to an async-compute queue.
  - If this workload is Graphics, then it may be a good candidate to be overlapped with async-compute work.

Rules.Name: No ZCULL, High EarlyZ
Explanation_Accumulated:
ZCULL happens between Coarse Raster and Fine Raster.  
EarlyZ happens between FineRaster and the Pixel Shader execution.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
Check that you are clearing your depth-stencil buffer with a ClearDepthStencilView command before rendering to it.  
Check that you are not changing the stencil-test state while rendering into the depth-stencil buffer.

Rules.Name: SM Warp Occupancy [Warps Per Cycle]
Explanation_Accumulated:
NVIDIA Ampere RTX GPUs have up to 48 warp slots per SM.  
NVIDIA Turing RTX GPUS have up to 32 warp slots per SM.  
Note: Increasing SM warp occupancy may not necessarily result in a performance gain.  
See https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/optimizing-vk-vkr-and-dx12-dxr-applications-using-nsight-graphics-gpu-trace-advanced-mode-metrics/ and https://www.gdcvault.com/browse/gdc-19/play/1026202.  
Less than 4 active warps per SM is a starving condition.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
The following strategies may be used to increase the SM warp occupancy:
- Reducing the SM warp launch stall reasons (see the SM Warp Occupancy section), typically register pressure
- Overlapping this workload with an indepedendent SM workload by using an Asynchronous Compute queue (for DX12 or VK)
- Reducing the number of DX12 ResouceBarriers or VK vkCmdPipelineBarrier commands

Rules.Name: Warp Stalled by L1TEX Long Scoreboard

Metrics.Name: Warps Issue Stalled Long Scoreboard L1 [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:
Percentage of cumulative warp cycles for warps waiting on a dependency on a memory read from:
- textures or buffers (SRVs)
- surfaces (UAVs or ROVs)
- local or global memory
Suggestion_Accumulated:
Run the Shader Profiler and locate which HLSL/GLSL instructions are causing most long_scoreboard stalls on their dependent instructions.  
* Try better hiding the latency of the L1TEX instructions:  
  - With other math instructions: try hoisting L1TEX instructions (i.e.: prefetch: move the texture fetches so they happen earlier in the program)  
  - With other L1TEX instructions: try batching likely hits (e.g. by grouping independent texture fetches in batches of 2 to 4 back-to-back instructions at the HLSL level)  
  - Removing unnecessary control flow that prevents L1TEX instructions from being batched
* Try reducing the latencies of the L1TEX instructions:  
  - Consider using more compact texture formats and/or reducing texture sizes  
  - Consider using Buffer SRV Loads instead of Buffer UAV Loads  
  - Consider increasing the L1TEX and L2 hit rates (see the L1TEX L2 section)

Rules.Name: Warp Stalled by No Instruction
Explanation_Accumulated: Percentage of cumulative warp cycles for warps waiting to be selected for instruction fetch, or waiting on an instruction cache miss.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
Reducing the number of SASS instructions per shader may help (for instance, by not unrolling certain loops).  
Reducing the number of active shaders may help (for instance, by doing lighting in a raygen shader instead of in hit shaders).  
Reducing ray-latency divergence may help, for instance by shortening rays and falling back to IBL (see SIGGRAPH 2020 talk: https://developer.nvidia.com/siggraph/2020/video/sigg01).  
Note: As long as the instructions that are never hit are in large chunks, they should not take up space in the SM instruction cache.

Rules.Name: Warp Stalled by Immediate Cache Miss
Explanation_Accumulated: IMC-cache misses can originate from immediate-indexed constant-buffer loads or from bindless-header loads or texture-header loads.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
Run the Shader Profiler and locate which HLSL instructions have most imc_miss stalls.  
Avoiding frequent constant-buffer updates between draw/dispatch calls may help.

- Enabling mipmapping and/or fetching coarser mip levels

- Making adjacent pixels fetch closer texels in memory
- For PSs, increasing the triangle size if some triangles are sub-pixel

  - In all cases, fetching 2D textures using a larger LOD bias (to fetch coarser mip levels) may help.

Rules.Name: Warp Stalled by L1TEX Long Scoreboard

Metrics.Name: Warps Issue Stalled Long Scoreboard L1 [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:
Percentage of cumulative warp cycles for warps waiting on a dependency on a memory read from:
- textures or buffers (SRVs)
- surfaces (UAVs or ROVs)
- local or global memory
Suggestion_Accumulated:
Run the Shader Profiler and locate which HLSL/GLSL instructions are causing most long_scoreboard stalls on their dependent instructions.  
* Try better hiding the latency of the L1TEX instructions:  
  - With other math instructions: try hoisting L1TEX instructions (i.e.: prefetch: move the texture fetches so they happen earlier in the program)  
  - With other L1TEX instructions: try batching likely hits (e.g. by grouping independent texture fetches in batches of 2 to 4 back-to-back instructions at the HLSL level)  
  - Removing unnecessary control flow that prevents L1TEX instructions from being batched
* Try reducing the latencies of the L1TEX instructions:  
  - Consider using more compact texture formats and/or reducing texture sizes  
  - Consider using Buffer SRV Loads instead of Buffer UAV Loads  
  - Consider increasing the L1TEX and L2 hit rates (see the L1TEX L2 section)

Rules.Name: Warp Stalled by L1TEX Long Scoreboard

Metrics.Name: Warps Issue Stalled Long Scoreboard L1 [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:

- local or global memory

Run the Shader Profiler and locate which HLSL/GLSL instructions are causing most long_scoreboard stalls on their dependent instructions.

  - With other math instructions: try hoisting L1TEX instructions (i.e.: prefetch: move the texture fetches so they happen earlier in the program)

Rules.Name: L1TEX L2 Hit Rates
Explanation_Accumulated:
If the L1TEX hit rate is poor, it causes more requests to go to the L2 cache.  
If the L2 hit rate is poor, it causes more requests to go to VRAM.  
A poor L2 hit rate is typically caused by the working set size of the GPU workload exceeding the L2 cache capacity.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
If the L1TEX hit rate is poor, the following changes may help:
- Enabling mipmapping and/or fetching coarser mip levels
- Using a smaller texture format (e.g. FP16 depths instead of FP32)
- Making adjacent pixels fetch closer texels in memory
- For PSs, increasing the triangle size if some triangles are sub-pixel
- For PSs, converting the PS to a CS and tweaking the thread group size
- For CSs, increasing the thread group size (see SIGGRAPH 2020 talk: https://developer.nvidia.com/siggraph/2020/video/sigg01)
- For CSs, if no async-compute queue is used, reducing the amount of allocated shared memory
If the L2 hit rate is poor:
  
  - For CSs with 2D thread groups, thread group ID swizzling may help (see https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/optimizing-compute-shaders-for-l2-locality-using-thread-group-id-swizzling/).
  - In all cases, fetching 2D textures using a larger LOD bias (to fetch coarser mip levels) may help.

Rules.Name: Warp Stalled by L1TEX Long Scoreboard

Metrics.Name: Warps Issue Stalled Long Scoreboard L1 [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:
Percentage of cumulative warp cycles for warps waiting on a dependency on a memory read from:
- textures or buffers (SRVs)
- surfaces (UAVs or ROVs)
- local or global memory
Suggestion_Accumulated:
Run the Shader Profiler and locate which HLSL/GLSL instructions are causing most long_scoreboard stalls on their dependent instructions.  
* Try better hiding the latency of the L1TEX instructions:  
  - With other math instructions: try hoisting L1TEX instructions (i.e.: prefetch: move the texture fetches so they happen earlier in the program)  
  - With other L1TEX instructions: try batching likely hits (e.g. by grouping independent texture fetches in batches of 2 to 4 back-to-back instructions at the HLSL level)  
  - Removing unnecessary control flow that prevents L1TEX instructions from being batched
* Try reducing the latencies of the L1TEX instructions:  
  - Consider using more compact texture formats and/or reducing texture sizes  
  - Consider using Buffer SRV Loads instead of Buffer UAV Loads  
  - Consider increasing the L1TEX and L2 hit rates (see the L1TEX L2 section)

Rules.Name: Warp Stalled by L1TEX Long Scoreboard

Metrics.Name: Warps Issue Stalled Long Scoreboard L1 [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:
Percentage of cumulative warp cycles for warps waiting on a dependency on a memory read from:
- textures or buffers (SRVs)
- surfaces (UAVs or ROVs)
- local or global memory
Suggestion_Accumulated:
Run the Shader Profiler and locate which HLSL/GLSL instructions are causing most long_scoreboard stalls on their dependent instructions.  
* Try better hiding the latency of the L1TEX instructions:  
  - With other math instructions: try hoisting L1TEX instructions (i.e.: prefetch: move the texture fetches so they happen earlier in the program)  
  - With other L1TEX instructions: try batching likely hits (e.g. by grouping independent texture fetches in batches of 2 to 4 back-to-back instructions at the HLSL level)  
  - Removing unnecessary control flow that prevents L1TEX instructions from being batched
* Try reducing the latencies of the L1TEX instructions:  
  - Consider using more compact texture formats and/or reducing texture sizes  
  - Consider using Buffer SRV Loads instead of Buffer UAV Loads  
  - Consider increasing the L1TEX and L2 hit rates (see the L1TEX L2 section)

Rules.Name: L1TEX L2 Hit Rates
Explanation_Accumulated:
If the L1TEX hit rate is poor, it causes more requests to go to the L2 cache.  
If the L2 hit rate is poor, it causes more requests to go to VRAM.  
A poor L2 hit rate is typically caused by the working set size of the GPU workload exceeding the L2 cache capacity.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
If the L1TEX hit rate is poor, the following changes may help:
- Enabling mipmapping and/or fetching coarser mip levels
- Using a smaller texture format (e.g. FP16 depths instead of FP32)
- Making adjacent pixels fetch closer texels in memory
- For PSs, increasing the triangle size if some triangles are sub-pixel
- For PSs, converting the PS to a CS and tweaking the thread group size
- For CSs, increasing the thread group size (see SIGGRAPH 2020 talk: https://developer.nvidia.com/siggraph/2020/video/sigg01)
- For CSs, if no async-compute queue is used, reducing the amount of allocated shared memory
If the L2 hit rate is poor:
  
  - For CSs with 2D thread groups, thread group ID swizzling may help (see https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/optimizing-compute-shaders-for-l2-locality-using-thread-group-id-swizzling/).
  - In all cases, fetching 2D textures using a larger LOD bias (to fetch coarser mip levels) may help.

Rules.Name: Active Threads Per Warp

Metrics.Name: Thread Inst Executed Pred On per Inst Executed [%]
SM Thread Inst Executed Pred On

Explanation_Accumulated:
Low active threads per warp can be caused by:
- Divergent branches, where an if-statement's condition resolves to a mixture of true and false across threads in the warp.
- Divergent control flow within warps (such as dynamic loops with different loop counts per thread).
- Dispatch commands launching less than 32 threads per thread group.
- In DispatchRays/vkCmdTraceRays, different rays executing different hit shaders within the same warp.  
Thread execution divergence due to dynamic control flow increases warp latencies, since all partially-taken branches must be executed with masked-out threads.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
In general, try to make all threads of the same warp take the same control-flow decision (dynamic branches or loops).  
In RayGen shaders, using the Shader Execution Reordering (SER) NvAPI. See https://developer.nvidia.com/sites/default/files/akamai/gameworks/ser-whitepaper.pdf

Rules.Name: SM Fully Idle

Metrics.Name: Unused Warp Slots in Idle SMs [%]

Explanation_Accumulated:
Percentage of the cycles where an SM has all of its warp slots empty (SM is fully idle).  
This may be due to the "Tail Effect", that is the warp occupancy going down at the end of a SM workload before a Wait For Idle.
Suggestion_Accumulated:
* Look at the SM Warp Occupancy metric graph in GPU Trace. If a significant tail is there, then:
  - See if a DX12 ResourceBarrier command can be removed at the end of the current workload, to let it execute concurrently with the next one, assuming that the current and next workloads are in the same subchannel (Graphics or Compute).
* If high, and resource dependencies permit, then:
  - If this workload is a Compute Shader, then it may be a good candidate for being moved to an async-compute queue.
  - If this workload is Graphics, then it may be a good candidate to be overlapped with async-compute work.
